description: The large native tussock grass of the Pampas, with tall silver flowering plumes.
nativeRange: Argentina, Uruguay, southern Brazil and nearby regions
ecology: Native grasses are the backbone of this landscape. They feed seed-eating birds, supply nesting material and shelter ground-dwelling insects.
wildlifeNotes: Seed for finches, sparrows and other seed-eaters. The dense tussock provides nesting material and habitat for ground-dwelling insects.
flowering: Tall plumes in late summer and autumn
safety: The leaf edges cut. Site it away from paths and places where people brush past.
